verdict.rationale: Requesty documents Load Balancing Policies that split requests across multiple models by user-defined weights, with sticky routing by trace_id or user_id. It also documents latency-based routing that picks the fastest model from real-time performance data. So weight and latency strategies are first-party, but cost-based balancing is never documented, and balancing is described across models rather than explicitly across deployments or API keys. missing for 10: cost-based routing/load balancing, explicit balancing across deployments or multiple keys, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can load-balance traffic across providers, deployments, or keys by weight, latency, or cost

citations.quote: Load Balancing Policies distribute your requests across multiple models based on weights you define.
Latency-Based Routing automatically selects the fastest model for each request based on real-time performance data.
Requests with the same trace_id or user_id always go to the same model.
